name: NY-15
label: Safe D

key_factors: No serious funded opposition; markets price 98% Democratic
model.rationale: The forecast rests on the district's D+27 lean plus Torres's incumbency advantage and overwhelming financial edge, with Polymarket pricing a Democratic win near certain. No polls or expert ratings justify moving away from the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Torres or an unusually strong independent challenge could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ritchie Torres seeks reelection in a Bronx-based district that leans Democratic by 27 points, one of the most heavily Democratic seats in the country. Torres is a well-established incumbent with a large financial advantage: he has raised nearly $7 million and holds $14 million on hand, while Republican nominee Stylo Sapaskis has reported no fundraising. Independent candidates, including Jose Vega, have raised only modest sums, and no outside group is spending against Torres.

With no general-election polling and no expert ratings available, the forecast relies on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold. Prediction markets agree, pricing a Torres win at roughly 98 percent. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
